title: FrigadeHQ/yogurt
why_read: A privacy-respecting, open-source local alternative to a commercial AI meeting-notes app, appealing to engineers wary of sending audio/transcripts to third-party clouds.
analysis: Yogurt positions itself as a free, open-source alternative to Granola, a popular AI note-taking tool, with the key differentiator being that processing happens locally rather than sending meeting data to external servers. This matters for privacy-conscious teams and companies with confidentiality requirements around meeting content, since local-only processing avoids a major vector of data exposure. Being cross-platform (Mac, Windows, Linux) and TypeScript-based also makes it accessible for broader developer contribution. The technical risk is whether local transcription and summarization quality can match cloud-based competitors, which isn't addressed by the description alone.
